thread:
lilia: :rotating_light: paging the oncall — we’re seeing a spike of NCCL errors on the tp shards for model-x in us-west-2, multiple tasks hitting COMMUNICATOR_TIMEOUT and occasional CUDA OOMs. customer-facing error rate ~6% and latency tail up.
sam: copying logs — attaching first failure snippet below
sam: ```
[2026-03-15 02:13:41] ERROR nccl: comm 0x7f9babc3 timeout at rank 2
[2026-03-15 02:13:42] WARN cuda: out of memory while allocating 1.2GiB
[2026-03-15 02:13:43] INFO containerd: restarting container model-x-worker-12
``` 
deepa: infra-bot reported node-flap on host gpu-12, kernel message: PCIe link reset then GPU driver recover
infra-bot: autoremediation triggered: drained node g-12, migrated live tasks off, restarted kubelet
max: observed pattern — collective fails start after a large micro-batch (>seq_len 2048) hits a barrier, then one rank OOMs and causes nccl timeout cascade. Likely KV cache growth + batch spike.
lilia: immediate mitigation suggestions? we need to keep customer impact low.
sam: short term: 1) enable routing fallback to single-gpu model-x-1g for new requests (no stateful sessions). 2) temporarily block large-batch requests (>512) at the routing layer. 3) restart communicator / force restart pods on remaining nodes to clear stuck NCCL communicators.
deepa: on it — applying route rule now: redirect model-x traffic to model-x-1g for tier=standard. also pushed a rate limit for batch_size>512 via gateway.
max: lowering default micro-batch size on serving config to 256 and enabling NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 for the worker pods might prevent hard hangs.
lilia: can we do graceful restart for pods that show COMM error rather than kill? risk is stuck communicator. I prefer drain+restart when COMM appears.
sam: agree. doing a rolling drain+restart of pods with COMM errors in the next 5m window. infra-bot will handle cordon/drain.
infra-bot: cordon g-12; draining 3 pods: model-x-worker-11/12/13; migrating live sessions where possible. Estimated completion 4m.
max: also toggled kernel param for nv_peer_mem backoff on g-13 to reduce nvlink retries (will monitor). Noted slight perf impact but reduces repeat resets.
lilia: customer comms — can someone draft an RCA blurb? need ETA for full restore.
sam: short blurb: "We identified a multi-GPU collective failure in the inference pool for model-x triggered by oversized micro-batches plus KV-cache growth causing OOM on one rank and cascading NCCL timeouts. We’ve activated a single-GPU fallback, blocked large batches, and are rolling restarts across affected hosts. Impact: ~6% errors, degraded P99 latency. ETA for full mitigation: 30–45 minutes while we validate stability." Thoughts?
deepa: solid. I’ll post to status page and mark as partial degradation. tagging customers on affected SLAs.
lilia: handoff notes for next oncall (cc @sam): 1) monitor error rate for 30m after rollouts; 2) keep batch blocker until we confirm no regressions; 3) collect full core dump from any remaining OOMs and upload to /mnt/incident-dumps/1952468000. 4) consider backfilling capacity from eu-west if us-west remains unstable.
sam: uploading collected logs and stacks to the incident folder now. pointer: s3://redwood-incident-logs/1952468000/
max: follow-up action items (post incident): - add a guard in serving runtime to cap per-request KV growth; - telemetry for seq_len distribution per route; - add an automatic fallback to single-GPU variant on first communicator timeout.
lilia: raising a follow-up ticket and assigning to eng-runtime/serving. Tagging @deepa for infra runbook updates.
pagerbot: oncall handoff scheduled at 03:00 UTC. Next responder: sam.
lilia: handoff summary (for next oncall): current state = mitigation applied (single-gpu fallback + batch cap + rolling restarts). customer impact reduced to ~1.2% errors and p99 recovering. keep an eye on nvlink resets and any node flaps. escalate to infra if another kernel PCIe reset appears.
sam: thanks all, will continue monitoring and update thread. :thumbsup:
